purpose: Pilocarpine is used to treat certain types of glaucoma by lowering the pressure inside your eye. It is also available as a pill to help with dry mouth caused by radiation therapy for head and neck cancer or by a condition called Sjogren's syndrome. Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision.
how_it_works: Pilocarpine works by mimicking a natural chemical in your body called acetylcholine. In your eye, it causes the tiny muscles to contract, which opens up the drainage channels so fluid can flow out more easily, lowering the pressure. When taken as a pill, it stimulates your saliva glands to produce more saliva, relieving dry mouth.
common_side_effects: Eye drops may cause blurred vision, especially at night or in dim light, eye irritation, redness, or a mild headache around your brow. The pill form can cause sweating, runny nose, chills, flushing, frequent urination, and nausea. These effects are usually mild and often improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have asthma, heart problems, kidney or liver disease, or stomach ulcers, as pilocarpine may worsen these conditions. Avoid driving at night or in low-light conditions when using the eye drops, since they can make it harder to see in the dark. Do not use more than prescribed, and keep all follow-up appointments so your doctor can monitor your eye pressure or overall response.
typical_dosing: Eye drops are usually placed in the affected eye 1 to 4 times daily as directed by your eye doctor. The oral tablet (Salagen) is typically taken 3 to 4 times a day with meals, usually 5 mg per dose. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions since your dose may be adjusted based on how you respond to the medication.
